title: RTEC AAP narrative / good-faith-effort history — June 2015 through June 2017
change_points: By June 2015 the large driver workforce is classified under Operatives rather than Service Workers, while Service Workers drops to two female employees; this is a major EEO-1 category mapping change that must not be mistaken for a collapse in driver headcount.
Veteran and individual-with-disability counts are integrated into the recurring job-group narrative.

Operatives/driver staffing grows from 139 in 2015 to 150 in 2016 and 157 in 2017; the 2015 and 2016 narratives set growth targets, while the 2017 narrative shifts to maintaining staffing with turnover-driven openings.
The source continues to evaluate female/minority placements against applicant bases and explicitly discusses minority turnover as a reason net representation can lag gross hires.

operatives_driver_history.result: 2 minorities and 18 females added; 1 minority lost to turnover; source says goal met
7 minorities and 18 females added; 3 minorities lost to turnover; source says goal exceeded
2 minorities and 28 females added; 3 minorities lost to turnover; source says goal met

organizational_mobility: First Mid-Level Officials/Managers remains heavily internally promoted: 90% in 2015, 80% in 2016, 78% in 2017.
Professionals remain small and male-only in these three narratives; 2017 explicitly anticipates one opening and states a good-faith intent to hire a female and/or minority.
Technician staffing alternates between vacant and one employee, with 2015 and 2017 anticipating an opening.
controls_and_interpretation: Annual narrative statements are historical AAP interpretations, not present-day staffing or hiring requirements.
Job-group changes must be analyzed as mapping/reclassification changes before comparing year-to-year headcounts.
All source percentages are preserved as printed. Extremely small minority placement/availability/applicant percentages require formula/format validation before quantitative reuse.
